purpose: svapaṭhanārtham vā paropakārārtham (for his own study, or for the benefit of others)
notes: The catalogue field 'VS 1875' is a transposition of 1857. The colophon reads saṃvat 1857 śāke 1722, and these agree (1722 + 135 = 1857). Phālguna śukla 13 of that year falls in about Feb/Mar 1801 CE. The weekday was not checked. 'svapanārthaṃ' is a corruption of svapaṭhanārthaṃ. 'Tāpitīra' probably means 'bank of the Tāpī (Tapti) river' in western India. The names Joītārāma and Dayārāma also point to Gujarat, so this copy was likely made outside Nepal; the place is left unnormalised. 'kalāsabhānātha' before Gaṇanātha looks like an epithet ('lord of the assembly of arts'), not part of the name. Fol. 29r6 has a corrupt scribal apology formula, 'adṛṣtabhāvāt matibharmād vā' (for matibhramād vā).
